description: Coastal Topographic Lidar is a web tool or resource listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by NOAA Office for Costal Management Digital Coast. LiDAR, or Light Detection and Ranging, is a remote sensing technology that uses lasers to measure vertical distances. The data can be used to create 3D maps. This site offers U.S. topographic data gathered by many groups using a variety of lidar sensors. Coverage: the United States, or as stated on the tool page. The toolkit lists hazards: Erosion and Shoreline Recession, Flooding – Coastal. Assets: Aquatic and Marine Resources, Natural Areas and Wildlife, Property, Transportation and Mobility, Urban Landscape and Tree Canopy, Water Infrastructure – Stormwater, Water Infrastructure – Wastewater. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the tool itself was not opened or run, its licence and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support climate-adaptation planning and exposure screening. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
